findings.basis: The source is one file: Motorola's carrier config as imported into LineageOS's android_device_motorola_lyriq (commit title names stock build V1TLS35.73-60-3-14). 2026-10-24 is the import date; the value's own age is not known, and stock itself was not read. Each listed block states the value explicitly for its exact network code and GID. Blocks 639, 644, 754, 755, 756, 761. Identity: Samsung's 2026-08 and 2026-09 rules list gid1 8030 and 9030 on 302-220 and 313-340 as Dish 5G, gid1 6532 on 313-340 as Dish 5G and gid1 6730 on 313-340 as Dish 5G Data only. Samsung's IMS data also carries gid1 8030 and 9030 with gid2 values as Dish US on 302-220, so these are GIDs of real Dish SIMs. The value: Google's dish5gsa_us sets allow_hold_call_during_emergency_bool false, rtt_supported_bool true and rtt_supported_while_roaming_bool true for every Dish GID it lists on 313-340 and for Dish's IMSI ranges; the same three values stand in each Motorola block here. Google's lane has no rule for these GIDs, so 'unset' here means Google does not list them, not that it states another value. These blocks are not marked: their code text reads back unchanged, so the LineageOS build applied them.
findings.effect: allow_hold_call_during_emergency_bool (CarrierConfigManager.java:2509-2516, default true at :12089). With false, TelephonyConnectionService hangs up every other TelephonyConnection and conference with cause OUTGOING_EMERGENCY_CALL_PLACED before it places the emergency call (TelephonyConnectionService.java:2392-2408; the same in recreateEmergencyConnection at 3545-3559; read at 3704-3714). Telecom's CallSequencingController also disconnects a managed ongoing call whose account carries false (CallSequencingController.java:1016-1037, 1097-1100); CallsManager.java:4623-4647 fills a missing key with true. The hangup marks the ImsPhoneCall DISCONNECTING (ImsPhoneCall.java:251-260), which is not alive (Call.java:53-55), so checkForDialIssues and prepareForDialing go straight to the dial (ImsPhoneCallTracker.java:2716-2734, 1648-1697). With true the tracker first holds the active call, and prepareForDialing throws 'cannot dial in current state' if that hold fails (1683-1689); a live foreground and background call stop the dial with ERROR_TOO_MANY_CALLS (2730-2733). No other reader of the key exists in the telephony, Telecom, IMS framework or ImsStack sources, the ocd fork included, so no TTY, RTT or priority path reads it. The cited files are the same on lineage-24.0. On a phone: a group A value is admitted only for the most specific profile that sets the key, else the Google-lane value, else Android's default (Serving.kt:405-440).
findings.risk: Against the default true these SIMs get now: other calls are dropped, not held, when an emergency call starts. The emergency call no longer waits on a hold that can fail, and two live calls no longer stop the dial. The cost falls on the other call, which the user cannot return to. Google ships the same behaviour for Dish, AT&T and others, and read 8c4ede5ebb12 passed it for Dish's IMSI ranges. No Google entry names these GIDs, one maker states the value, and nobody tested it on this stack. By its name a Dish 5G Data only SIM makes no voice calls, so there the value would do nothing.

notes: Proceed. False takes the hold step out of the emergency dial. The value is the one Google ships for the same operator, on GIDs Samsung names as Dish. Read, not tested.
